mechanism: Per enabled TF (M15/H1/H4/D1), GetStructureBias returns +1/0/−1 from a three-bar staircase (rising highs+lows or falling highs+lows) with close-price fallback; HI = sum(bias_i * weight_i) / sum(weights), normalized to [−1,+1]. Strong/Moderate thresholds (defaults 0.8/0.4) classify strong bull/bear, moderate, or weak/neutral consensus.
data_needed: OHLC on each enabled TF; user weights and enable flags; StrongThreshold, ModerateThreshold
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 75 (1s) Index live; GBPUSD H1 backtest; monitored TFs M15, H1, H4, D1
why_new_for_mis: Turns subjective multi-TF agreement into a single continuous regime-alignment sensor MIS can gate on, with explicit per-TF structural votes rather than indicator mashups.
quote: the Multi‑Timeframe Harmony Index (HI) addresses this difficulty by condensing per‑timeframe structural bias into a single normalized numeric measure between –1.0 and +1.0.

idea_name: EMA-smoothed HI threshold-cross and HTF bias-flip change sensor
mechanism: HI is EMA-smoothed (alpha = 2/(HI_EMA_Period+1)); alerts fire on (1) HI crossing ±StrongThreshold from a weaker state and (2) H4 or D1 structural bias flipping sign. Buy/sell arrows plot only on strong threshold crossings with dedup per bar.
data_needed: Raw HI series; HI_EMA_Period; prior HI and prior H4/D1 biases; EnableAlerts/EnableSignals
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same multi-TF stack; Volatility 75 and GBPUSD H1
why_new_for_mis: Separates regime level (HI) from regime-change events (threshold cross + higher-TF flip)—MIS can subscribe to flip events as structural regime-change triggers independent of lower-TF noise.
quote: The second is Higher‑Timeframe Bias Flips, where the bias for H4 or D1 changes sign—flipping, for example, from bullish to bearish or vice versa.

mechanism: Each slot emits SIG_BUY/+1, SIG_SELL/−1, or NEUTRAL/0 from tool-specific rules (EMA slope, ADX>25, RSI extremes, MACD zero-line, Stoch/Momentum/CCI/Williams thresholds; ATR/BB contribute volatility context only). ComputeOverall multiplies by group weight Trend×3, Momentum×2, Volatility×1 and signs the sum as BUY/SELL/NEUTRAL.
data_needed: Indicator handles for EMA50/200, ADX14, RSI14/28, MACD(12,26,9), Stoch(5,3), Momentum14, CCI20, Williams%R14, ATR14, BB(20,2); timer refresh
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any MT5 symbol/timeframe via InpTF (default PERIOD_CURRENT)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a portable three-family voting template where trend dominates, momentum supports, and volatility contextualizes—explicit group weighting for fused regime readout.
quote: trend indicators carry the highest influence… momentum indicators exert moderate influence; and volatility indicators contribute a lighter weight

mechanism: Dashboard profile modes ALL/TREND/MOMENTUM/VOL filter which IndicatorSlots update and display; only slots in the active profile are refreshed each OnTimer cycle, so the overall vote can be recomputed under a focused family lens.
data_needed: Slot group tags (0/1/2); currentProfile enum; same indicator buffers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart-attached EA; user switches profiles live
why_new_for_mis: Frames sensing as switchable analytical apertures—MIS can maintain parallel trend-only vs momentum-only vs vol-only state streams without rebuilding the feature set.
quote: Traders can toggle between four profile modes: ALL… TREND… MOMENTUM… and VOL… depending on the immediate question they need answered.

mechanism: Closed-bar engine requires all three: SMA(30) structural bias (price below SMA for bullish setup / above for bearish), RVGI main×signal crossover for momentum turn, and CCI(14) exhaustion gate—bullish when CCI returns from ≤−100, bearish when returning from ≥+100 (design framework). ATR or swing extremes size stops/targets.
data_needed: OHLC for manual RVGI/CCI; SMA and ATR handles; CCI ±100 thresholds; RVI smooth period
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD M1 buy example; Volatility 75 (1s) Index M1 sell example
why_new_for_mis: Packages structure + momentum flip + statistical exhaustion as a single change sensor for mean-reversion regime turns—MIS can treat the triple AND as a high-precision reversal event.
quote: SMA defines the structural bias, RVGI confirms the momentum shift, and CCI confirms that price has exhausted its extreme.

idea_name: Closed-bar classical candlestick pattern library as sentiment footprint sensor
mechanism: Modular detectors (Doji body≤10% range, Hammer/Shooting Star wick geometry, engulfing body containment, Morning/Evening Star, Three Soldiers/Crows, etc.) run on CopyRates; search mode targets one pattern, scan-all marks every library match over LookbackPeriod; real-time mode evaluates last completed bar with per-pattern AlertCooldown.
data_needed: OHLC MqlRates window; pattern-specific ratio thresholds; LookbackPeriod, MaxDisplayPatterns, AlertCooldown
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 75 (1s) Index M5 (52 Bullish Engulfing in 1000 bars); also EURUSD, USDJPY, NZDUSD
why_new_for_mis: Treats named candle formations as a discrete event vocabulary of buyer/seller footprints MIS can count, co-occur, or sequence rather than only continuous oscillators.
quote: candlesticks are, in many ways, the true footprints of price action. They reflect where the market has been and, quite often, hint at where it might go next.

idea_name: Dual HTF candle-direction alignment with pip threshold
mechanism: CandleDirection of current TF, HTF1, and HTF2 (bullish/bearish from open vs close) must agree and price move must exceed MinPipsForSignal before firing MTF CONFIRM BULL/BEAR; optional AlertOnOpposite when HTF1==HTF2 but current disagrees. Overlays draw accurate HTF bodies/wicks on the working chart.
data_needed: OHLC on current, HTF1, HTF2; MinPipsForSignal; RefreshSeconds; optional sound/push/mail
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Example EURUSD M15 with HTF1=H1, HTF2=M30; also USDJPY session walkthrough
why_new_for_mis: Senses multi-horizon directional regime by requiring candle-bias agreement across three clocks plus a minimum displacement filter—complement to weighted HI with explicit visual HTF structure.
quote: If all three share the same direction—meaning current price action harmonizes with HTF1 and HTF2—the analyzer recognizes this as a technical confirmation.

idea_name: CPI-validated session boundary acceptance vs rejection
mechanism: Tokyo/London/NY session rectangles from broker HH:MM windows; SessionRangeFromShift builds analytical high/low excluding evaluation bars. Acceptance: break candle closes beyond boundary with |CPI|≥InpStrongThreshold, then confirmation retests and holds beyond. Rejection: confirmation trades beyond then closes back inside with CPI threshold flip (e.g. bearish rej: cpi1≤−strong while cpi2 not strongly negative) plus optional wick filter. Once-per-session-per-side flags suppress repeats.
data_needed: OHLC with absolute bar times; session start/end HH:MM; CalcCPI(high,low,close) in [−1,+1]; InpMinRangePoints noise gate; strong/neutral CPI thresholds
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; XAUUSD H1 Strategy Tester
why_new_for_mis: Converts session highs/lows into liquidity memory zones and uses close-location pressure (CPI) to classify acceptance vs rejection—session microstructure sensing MIS typically lacks.
quote: Acceptance occurs when price moves beyond the level and sustains above or below it… Rejection occurs when price tests the level but fails to maintain pressure beyond it, rotating back into the earlier range.

idea_name: Candle Pressure Index as internal close-location sensor
mechanism: CPI measures where the close sits inside the candle’s high–low range and normalizes to [−1,+1], exposing buying/selling dominance beyond candle color; low-range bars below InpMinRangePoints are gated as noise. Used as the pressure layer on session interactions.
data_needed: Per closed candle high, low, close; minimum range in points
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD/XAUUSD H1 session tests; builds on Part 55 CPI indicator
why_new_for_mis: Provides a scale-free intra-bar pressure feature MIS can stream alongside OHLC for absorption/commitment sensing at any boundary, not only sessions.
quote: The CPI values are normalized within a fixed range of −1 to +1, allowing pressure strength to be compared consistently across candles.

mechanism: Closed-candle features: baseline AvgRange(lookback), recent vs previous window range for shrink ratio, lastRange, CLV=(2C−H−L)/(H−L), mean CLV, swingScore from last two swing highs/lows. Classify in order: Expansion if lastRange≥avgRange×InpExpansionMult and |lastCLV|≥InpCLVStrong; else Compression if recentAvg≤prevAvg×InpRangeShrinkRatio; else Trend if |meanCLV|≥bias and |swingScore|≥min; else Transition. Non-trading descriptive EA.
data_needed: OHLC closed bars; InpLookbackBars, InpCompressionBars, InpTrendBars, InpSwingLeftRight; thresholds InpRangeShrinkRatio≈0.70, InpExpansionMult≈1.80, InpCLVStrong≈0.60
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1 Strategy Tester; EURUSD M5 live
why_new_for_mis: Core MIS regime primitive: separates volatility freedom (compression→expansion) from directional structure (trend) with an explicit residual Transition state—all from pure price action.
quote: Solid—Compression; Liquid—Transition; Gas—Expansion… Trend is evaluated independently of the volatility-based analogy.

idea_name: Relative range-shrink compression and CLV-gated expansion
mechanism: Compression is relative (recent window avg range vs equal prior window), so it adapts across symbols/TFs without fixed pip floors. Expansion requires both abnormal range multiple of baseline ATR-like avg and decisive close location (|CLV| strong), rejecting wide mid-close bars as false energy releases.
data_needed: CandleRange series; dual-window averages; last CLV
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS adaptive vol-contraction and vol-release sensors that self-normalize to recent behavior and demand close conviction—stronger than raw ATR spikes alone.
quote: Because this comparison is relative, it adapts naturally across symbols and timeframes by measuring the market against its own recent behavior.

idea_name: Geometric asymmetry pre-breakout bias from fractal consolidation
mechanism: Bill Williams 5-bar fractals → three alternating swings qualify a range (min bars, height≤ATR×cap, recent side-zone touches). Inside range, geometry votes: lengthRatio≥InpLenRatioMin, slopeRatio≥InpSlopeRatioMin, timeRatio≤InpTimeCompressionMax; bias locks when votes≥InpMinGeometryVotes and last leg ends near boundary. Breakout signal only on close beyond locked high/low ± buffer.
data_needed: OHLC; ATR(14); fractal swings; InpLenRatioMin≈1.35, InpSlopeRatioMin≈1.15, InpTimeCompressionMax≈0.95, InpMinGeometryVotes≈2; lock/cooldown bars
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 strongest; AUDUSD visual tester; majors with calibrated params
why_new_for_mis: Senses impending range-to-trend change from internal leg imbalance (distance, slope, time compression) before the boundary break—early regime-transition cue for MIS.
quote: GA therefore reflects pre-breakout bias, not trend confirmation, and is evaluated only after a valid range and objective swing structure have been established.

idea_name: ATR-filtered raw-swing slanted support/resistance structure sensor
mechanism: FindSignificantSwings: local dominance over ±SwingLookback neighbors; swing size vs MinSwingSize or currentATR×0.8. Chronologically ordered descending highs scored for resistance and ascending lows for support by touch count within deviation, recency, MinTouchPointsRequired; best lines drawn as OBJ_TREND rays preserving exact market slope (no regression).
data_needed: OHLC rates; optional ATR(14); SwingLookback, MinSwingSize/ATR factor, MinTouchPointsRequired
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 live ~12h observation and historical replay
why_new_for_mis: Produces objective slanted structural rails MIS can treat as dynamic S/R features—complementing horizontal levels with slope-aware containment sensing.
quote: Instead of depending on an indicator to define swings, the current tool derives swing points directly from raw price action.

idea_name: Three-swing validated slanted trendline breakout cross sensor
mechanism: Best resistance/support lines require a third swing within ThirdSwingToleranceATR of the line (LinePriceAtTime interpolation); breakout only when price crosses from one side to the other (close or wick + BreakoutBufferPoints), not mere touches—bullish on cross above validated slanted resistance, bearish below slanted support.
data_needed: Validated swing arrays; ATR for tolerance/size; BreakoutUseClose, BreakoutBufferPoints; MinTouchPointsRequired (default 3)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 Strategy Tester; XAUUSD H1 volatile backtest
why_new_for_mis: Elevates slanted-structure break to a change event only after three-swing confirmation—filters coincidental geometry and touch noise for MIS breakout sensing.
quote: While two points are sufficient to define a line geometrically, they offer no proof that price respects it. The third swing provides that confirmation

idea_name: Adaptive parallel-channel score and dual-side breakout sensor
mechanism: Exhaustive swing-high/low pairs with slope similarity (MaxSlopeDifference), ATR-normalized MinChannelWidth, touch counts on both rails, recency bonus → best Channel scored and typed ASCENDING/DESCENDING/HORIZONTAL. Breakouts monitor both boundaries with strict cross mode, strength ATR floors, optional liquidity-sweep filter (wick beyond but close inside), volatility-expansion (ATR_now/ATR_10), structural break vs last swing, channel-type directional filter, and optional retest pending state.
data_needed: SwingPoint arrays; ATR(14); channel search params; BreakoutMinStrengthATR, UseLiquiditySweepFilter, UseVolatilityExpansion, UseRetestMode
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 live demo (descending channel break ~18 Feb 2026); EURUSD H1 backtest
why_new_for_mis: Full two-sided containment regime (channel) plus filtered escape events—MIS gets equidistant structure state and breakout quality (sweep vs expansion vs retest) in one stack.
quote: By tracking both sides of the channel, the framework ensures no significant movement is missed.

idea_name: Liquidity-sweep vs volatility-expansion breakout authenticity filters
mechanism: UseLiquiditySweepFilter flags isSweep when high/low pierces channel rail+buffer but close remains inside—suppressing those as false breakouts. UseVolatilityExpansion requires atrNow/atr10 ≥ MinVolatilityExpansion so accepted breaks coincide with expanding volatility.
data_needed: Bar high/low/close vs projected rail; atrBuffer[0] and atrBuffer[10]
why_new_for_mis: Explicitly separates liquidity-hunt wicks from volatility-backed structural breaks—actionable liquidity vs true regime-escape discrimination for MIS.
quote: isSweepUp = (high > upper1 + buf) && (close <= upper1 + buf); … volExpanded = (atrNow / atr10) >= MinVolatilityExpansion

idea_name: Rising/falling wedge convergence and apex-ahead compression sensor
mechanism: Confirmed pivots (PivotLeft/Right) with MinTouches per boundary; upperSlope and lowerSlope from earliest-to-latest pivot pairs. Rising wedge: both slopes >0 and lowerSlope>upperSlope; falling: both <0 and upperSlope<lowerSlope. Apex projection must lie ahead of currentBar; overlap rejection keeps one clean structure. Compression geometry (converging, not parallel) distinguishes wedges from channels.
data_needed: Pivot highs/lows arrays; MinTouches; slope math; current bar index for apex check
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, XAUUSD; M15–H4; live EURUSD M30 demo
why_new_for_mis: Detects directional compression (converging rails + future apex) as a distinct vol-regime precursor to expansion—MIS can track wedge state separately from parallel channels.
quote: The convergence itself is what differentiates a wedge from a parallel channel. In a channel, boundaries remain equidistant. In a wedge, they do not.

mechanism: After formation, Update projects UpperPriceAt/LowerPriceAt each bar; rising wedge expected resolution is lowerBreak (isBroken), opposite upperBreak or collapsed rails marks isFailed; falling wedge mirrors. Labels flip to BREAKOUT or FAILED only on decisive close beyond boundary ± Point()*3 buffer—reactive, not anticipatory.
data_needed: Active Wedge slopes/anchors; current close; isBroken/isFailed flags
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30 live animation with multiple independent resolutions
why_new_for_mis: Turns pattern lifecycle into a binary resolution sensor (expected expansion vs invalidation)—MIS can log compression→break vs compression→fail as regime-change outcomes.
quote: Importantly, the example highlights that the system does not anticipate breakouts—it reacts only once boundary conditions are decisively met.
